summary.headline: RoboColosseum reveals policy rankings don't transfer across robot bodies; Agent skills ecosystem crystallizes around Claude Code and MCP as three skills repos hit trending simultaneously; Kimi K3 2.78T runs on 8 GB CPU in pure C99
summary.body:
Today's research landscape is dominated by a reckoning in physical AI evaluation. RoboColosseum (arXiv:2611.02497), a 29-author distributed study across 124 real-robot sites and 5,699 pairwise comparisons, finds that policy rankings agree only weakly across different robot embodiments (Kendall W = 0.24). GR00T N1.7 leads on the SO-101 arm after fine-tuning, while pi0.5 dominates on Franka and Bimanual-YAM — meaning no single policy is universally best. The implication is that existing leaderboard culture in robotics may be systematically misleading.

On the agent-infrastructure front, a skills economy is crystallizing in real time. Three separate "skills" repositories (mattpocock/skills, anthropics/skills, scenario-labs/skills) hit GitHub trending simultaneously, with virgiliojr94/book-to-skill adding 1,421 stars in a single day for its ability to convert any technical book PDF into a Claude Code skill. Vercel Labs' agent-desktop (4,490 stars) and NVIDIA's auto-ontology (3,767 stars) further signal that the agent middleware layer is consolidating. Meanwhile, Voluntary Servitude (arXiv:2611.04393, NeurIPS 2026 main track) shows that attackers can weaponize an agent's own harm-avoidance to bypass prompt injection detectors — a critical security finding that coincides with microsoft/agent-governance-toolkit trending at 442 stars today.

On the model side, Qwen3.8-27B continues to dominate with 19,400 likes and 7.8M downloads, while LiquidAI's LFM3 family spans three modalities (text, any-to-any, vision-language) in the same trending week — suggesting a coordinated full-stack model release. The week's most technically audacious demo: FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c runs the 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 MoE on a single CPU in just 8.24 GB of RAM using portable C99 — no BLAS, no GPU, no framework dependency.

researcher_notes:
**The agent skills layer is crystallizing as AI's next platform moment.** Three separate "skills" repositories hit GitHub trending simultaneously today — mattpocock/skills (2,498 stars), anthropics/skills (793 stars today), and scenario-labs/skills (448 stars) — while virgiliojr94/book-to-skill's explosive 1,421-star day signals the community is rushing to build a skills economy on top of Claude Code and similar agent frameworks. This is the npm/PyPI moment for the agent era: the question has shifted from "can agents use tools?" to "how do we package, discover, and compose agent capabilities at scale?"

**RoboColosseum's finding that policy rankings don't transfer across robot bodies (Kendall W = 0.24) is quietly devastating for the VLA evaluation culture.** The 29-author study spans 124 real-world sites — not simulations — and finds that GR00T N1.7 leads on SO-101, pi0.5 leads on Franka and Bimanual-YAM, while frontier AI agents only rival specialized VLAs under fine-tuning. The honest takeaway: a single "best policy" leaderboard is scientifically indefensible. This mirrors the 2020 ImageNet reckoning, and robotics researchers should prepare for a methodological overhaul in how results are reported.

**Voluntary Servitude (2611.04393, NeurIPS 2026 main track) is the week's most important sleeper hit for the security community.** The paper shows that an attacker can steer an AI agent through the agent's own harm-avoidance mechanisms — using safety as a control surface rather than a shield. This bypasses standard prompt injection detectors because the attack exploits the model's own compliance behavior. With microsoft/agent-governance-toolkit trending and thedotmack/claude-mem's persistent session memory becoming popular, the attack surface of long-running agents is growing faster than defenses.

**LiquidAI's LFM3 family appearing across three separate model categories (1.7B text, Omni-2B any-to-any, VL-2B vision-language) in the same trending week is a signal of coordinated full-stack positioning.** Unlike point-solution releases, LFM3 is clearly designed to cover every modality at the efficiency tier. With Kimi-K3.1-Pro from Moonshot also trending strongly (1,540 likes, 18K downloads), and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 holding second position (5,365 likes), the mid-tier open-weight race has never been more competitive — and Qwen3.8-27B's 19,400 likes suggest it still leads.

**The 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 running on a single CPU in 8.24 GB of RAM (FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c) deserves more attention than its 653 stars suggest.** Using pure C99 without BLAS, framework, or GPU, the repo achieves this through aggressive MoE sparsity (only ~8B active parameters per token) combined with efficient C-level memory management. This isn't just a curiosity — it's a proof-of-concept that the "you need a GPU cluster for trillion-parameter models" assumption is now falsifiable. Watch for this technique to influence both edge deployment and the design of next-generation MoE routing algorithms.

papers.title: RoboColosseum: Evaluating Physical Intelligence at Scale In-The-Wild
papers.summary: A distributed evaluation framework running 5,699 pairwise policy comparisons across 124 real-robot sites spanning four embodiments. The key finding is that policy rankings agree only weakly across different robot bodies (Kendall W = 0.24), undermining single-embodiment leaderboards.
key_findings: GR00T N1.7 leads on SO-101 arm after fine-tuning; pi0.5 leads on Franka and Bimanual-YAM
Frontier AI agents rival specialized VLA policies only under zero-shot conditions on specific embodiments
Policy rankings show Kendall W = 0.24 correlation across robot types — essentially uncorrelated
All systems struggle to reliably complete open-world manipulation tasks

papers.title: Voluntary Servitude: Weaponized Safety Warning Mechanisms for Controlling AI Agents
papers.summary: A NeurIPS 2026 main-track security paper demonstrating that adversaries can steer AI agents by exploiting the agents' own harm-avoidance mechanisms, bypassing standard prompt injection detectors by using the safety layer as a control surface.
key_findings: Agents can be controlled via their own safety warning triggers — a novel attack vector distinct from direct prompt injection
Standard injection detectors fail to catch this class of attack because it exploits model compliance rather than instruction override
Attack is applicable across multiple agent frameworks
Defense requires rethinking how safety warnings are architecturally isolated from task execution

papers.title: Strategist: Evolving Reasoning with Agents
papers.summary: A NeurIPS 2026 paper proposing a meta-agent that evolves inference strategies across tasks, storing them as reusable code blueprints. The system learns which reasoning patterns work for which task types and routes future queries accordingly.
key_findings: Meta-agent stores inference strategies as executable code blueprints that can be reused across task instances
Outperforms static chain-of-thought on diverse task distributions by adapting reasoning style to problem type
Strategy evolution enables continuous improvement without retraining the base model

papers.title: Phantom Consensus: Measuring Social Reasoning in Multi-Agent LLM Decision-Making
papers.summary: A NeurIPS 2026 SocialAgent Workshop paper examining how multi-agent LLM systems reach false consensus. The study finds that revealing agents' private decisions before group deliberation significantly reduces phantom consensus failures.
key_findings: Multi-agent LLM systems frequently produce phantom consensus — apparent agreement masking underlying disagreement
Showing agents' private decisions before deliberation reduces false consensus rate substantially
Social reasoning failures are distinct from individual reasoning failures and require dedicated measurement frameworks

papers.title: AIM: Adaptive Interaction in Multi-Agent Debate for Multimodal LLM Inference
papers.summary: A NeurIPS 2026 paper studying how agents exchange evidence during multi-agent debate for multimodal reasoning tasks. The adaptive interaction scheme improves inference quality by selectively routing visual vs. textual evidence between agents.
key_findings: Evidence routing strategy between agents matters as much as individual agent capability
Adaptive interaction outperforms fixed debate protocols on multimodal benchmarks
Visual evidence benefits from different routing patterns than textual reasoning chains

papers.title: Democratizing Robot-Use Agents: Open-Weight Zero-Shot Manipulation at Proprietary Scale
papers.summary: A unified harness enabling open-weight robot-use agents to compete with proprietary models in zero-shot manipulation tasks. With 48 HuggingFace upvotes, the paper proposes standardized protocols that close the gap between open-source and commercial robot agent performance.
key_findings: Open-weight agents achieve competitive zero-shot manipulation performance against proprietary systems under the unified harness
Standardized evaluation protocol enables fair comparison across heterogeneous agent architectures
The harness is released open-source with adapters for major robot embodiments

papers.title: VisSearch-Bench: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents on Visual Search Tasks
papers.summary: A benchmark of 204 visual search tasks evaluating multimodal agents equipped with search tools. Even the best current systems solve only 26.47% of tasks, revealing a large gap in visual information retrieval for agentic AI.
key_findings: Best-performing multimodal agents with search tools solve only 26.47% of 204 visual search tasks
Visual search remains far harder than text search for current agent architectures
Common failure modes: incorrect visual grounding, over-reliance on text search over visual inspection

papers.title: Frontier3DBench: Benchmarking Coding Agents for 3D Creation
papers.summary: A benchmark evaluating AI coding agents on 3D content creation tasks including modeling, rigging, and scene composition. Trending on HuggingFace Daily Papers, it establishes baselines for 3D programming agents.
key_findings: Current coding agents show highly variable performance on 3D tasks compared to 2D coding benchmarks
3D-specific reasoning (spatial, procedural geometry) remains a challenge for LLM-based agents
Establishes standardized tasks spanning modeling, physics simulation, and rendering code

papers.title: Scaling Laws for Sparse Autoencoder Training Data
papers.summary: An arXiv cs.LG paper (2611.07756) establishing how performance of sparse autoencoders (SAEs) scales with training data volume. Important for mechanistic interpretability research as SAEs are used to extract human-interpretable features from model activations.
key_findings: SAE quality scales predictably with training data volume following a power law
Data scaling yields greater gains than architectural scaling for SAEs at comparable compute
Findings have direct implications for cost-effective interpretability research

papers.title: Reasoning Through Executable Visual State Abstractions
papers.summary: An arXiv cs.CV paper (2611.07397) proposing executable visual state abstractions as an intermediate representation for multi-step visual reasoning. The model converts visual inputs into runnable code-like state descriptions before reasoning.
key_findings: Executable state abstractions improve multi-step visual reasoning accuracy over direct pixel-to-answer approaches
State representation can be run to verify consistency, enabling self-correction
Outperforms chain-of-thought on structured spatial reasoning tasks

papers.title: Long-Tail Detection Data Synthesis via Diffusion Models
papers.summary: An arXiv cs.CV paper (2611.07553) using diffusion models to synthesize training data for rare object detection categories, addressing long-tail imbalance without manual annotation.
key_findings: Diffusion-synthesized images for rare categories significantly improve rare-class detection recall
Synthesis pipeline is label-conditioned and requires no additional annotation
Gains are consistent across LVIS and custom long-tail benchmarks

papers.title: FlashSSM-3D: A Distilled State Space Model for Lightning-Fast Dense 3D Reconstruction
papers.summary: A NeurIPS 2026 paper distilling state space models into an efficient architecture for dense 3D reconstruction. Part of UCF IAI's 29-paper NeurIPS 2026 cohort, targeting deployment-time efficiency for 3D scene understanding.
key_findings: Knowledge distillation from larger SSMs to a compact 3D reconstruction model achieves significantly faster inference
Maintains quality comparable to full-sized models on standard 3D benchmarks
Enables real-time dense reconstruction on edge devices

models.name: Qwen3.8-27B
models.description: The dominant multimodal model this week with 19,400 likes and 7.8M downloads. An image-text-to-text model supporting both vision and language tasks, with the TURBO-Fable GGUF quantization variant adding another 1.5M downloads.

models.name: LTX-2.5
models.description: Second most popular model by likes (10,887) and second by downloads (2.6M), LTX-2.5 is a highly capable image-to-video and video-to-video generation model. Its strong community adoption indicates it may be the leading open-weight video generation model currently available.

models.name: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017
models.description: DeepSeek's latest flash-tier multimodal model with 5,365 likes and 259K downloads (up from 4,314 likes on Nov 1), trending strongly. Multiple GGUF quantization variants have accumulated millions of additional downloads, confirming widespread deployment.

models.name: SAM3
models.description: Meta's SAM3 (Segment Anything Model 3) for video segmentation has accumulated 6,013 likes and 1.9M downloads, indicating strong adoption for video understanding and annotation workflows.

models.name: NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe-30B-A4B
models.description: NVIDIA's 30B MoE speech recognition model with only 4B active parameters per inference step. With 3,078 likes and 61K downloads, it represents state-of-the-art efficient ASR at large scale.

models.name: Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B
models.description: Mistral's latest large-scale model with a 1 trillion parameter count and 52B active parameters, targeting the top performance tier. With 1,626 likes and 10K downloads, it's newly released and trending.

models.name: Kimi-K3.1-Pro
models.description: Moonshot's latest multimodal model with 1,540 likes and 18K downloads. Part of the Kimi K3 family (the same architecture that runs in 8GB C99 as a demo), K3.1-Pro is the productionized version for general multimodal inference.

models.name: LFM3-1.7B
models.description: The smallest model in LiquidAI's new LFM3 (Liquid Foundation Model 3) family. With 1,530 likes and 66K downloads, it leads the efficiency tier this week. The simultaneous release of LFM3-Omni-2B and LFM3-VL-2B signals a full-modality push.

models.name: FLUX.3 Image Klein (ComfyUI)
models.description: Black Forest Labs' FLUX.3 image-to-image model packaged for ComfyUI workflows. With 2,631 likes (Nov 7) and 1.1M downloads, it maintains strong community adoption for image editing workflows.

models.name: Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder
models.description: A fine-tuned Qwen3.5 4B model specialized for text-to-3D code generation (ThreeJS). With 801 likes and 190K downloads, it reflects growing demand for LLMs that can directly generate 3D scene descriptions and procedural geometry code.

models.name: Unlimited-OCR-2
models.description: Baidu's second-generation unlimited OCR model for document parsing. With 638 likes and 310K downloads, it serves strong demand for multilingual OCR in enterprise document processing pipelines.

models.name: LFM3-Omni-2B
models.description: The any-to-any variant in LiquidAI's LFM3 family, handling arbitrary modality combinations at 2B parameters. Its simultaneous release with LFM3-1.7B and LFM3-VL-2B confirms a coordinated multi-modal product launch.

trending_repos.name: vercel-labs/agent-desktop
trending_repos.description: A computer use CLI for AI agents, enabling automated desktop interactions. With 4,490 stars it's the top trending AI-infrastructure repo this week, reflecting demand for agents that can operate GUIs without browser automation.

trending_repos.name: NVIDIA/auto-ontology
trending_repos.description: A Python framework for graph-based semantic reasoning layers for LLM and agent workflows, targeting deterministic query generation and improved context retrieval. 3,767 stars signals strong enterprise interest in structured reasoning for agents.

trending_repos.name: D4Vinci/Scrapling
trending_repos.description: A unified web scraping framework covering single requests through full-scale crawls. With 3,632 stars it's trending for use in agent data-gathering pipelines requiring reliable structured web extraction.

trending_repos.name: mattpocock/skills
trending_repos.description: An engineering skills collection for AI agents, extracted from the author's .agents directory. With 2,498 stars, it's part of the emerging skills-economy layer for Claude Code and similar agent frameworks.

trending_repos.name: thedotmack/claude-mem
trending_repos.description: Persistent memory across AI agent sessions — captures agent activity, compresses it with AI, and feeds relevant context back into later sessions. Supports Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Copilot, and others. 2,241 stars.

trending_repos.name: virgiliojr94/book-to-skill
trending_repos.description: Converts any technical book PDF into a Claude Code skill, enabling rapid knowledge injection into agent workflows. An explosive 1,421 stars gained today confirms strong community demand for the skills packaging layer.

trending_repos.name: anthropics/skills
trending_repos.description: Anthropic's official public repository for Agent Skills. Trending at 793 stars gained today, it represents Anthropic's platform-level investment in a skills marketplace alongside the Claude Code ecosystem.

trending_repos.name: microsoft/agent-governance-toolkit
trending_repos.description: An AI agent governance toolkit covering policy enforcement, zero-trust identity, execution sandboxing, and reliability engineering for autonomous AI agents. 442 stars today, directly relevant to the Voluntary Servitude security paper.

trending_repos.name: max-sixty/worktrunk
trending_repos.description: A CLI for Git worktree management designed for parallel AI agent workflows. 964 stars. Addresses the emerging pattern of multiple agents working concurrently on different branches of the same repository.

trending_repos.name: FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c
trending_repos.description: Runs the 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 MoE model on a single CPU in just 8.24 GB of RAM using portable C99 — no BLAS, framework, or GPU required. 653 stars, but technically the most remarkable demo of the week. Proves trillion-parameter inference is possible on commodity hardware via MoE sparsity.

trending_repos.name: microsoft/VibeVoice
trending_repos.description: Microsoft's open-source voice AI project, gaining 336 stars today. Provides frontier-quality voice synthesis and recognition for integration into agent pipelines and applications.

trending_repos.name: scenario-labs/skills
trending_repos.description: Agent skills for generating images, video, audio, and 3D through the Scenario MCP, plus expert workflows for Blender, Maya, ZBrush, Unreal, and Unity. 448 stars. Bridges the AI agent skills ecosystem with professional 3D/creative tool pipelines.

themes.name: Agent Infrastructure & Skills Economy
themes.description: The agent skills layer is crystallizing as a platform. Three skills repos hit trending simultaneously, vercel-labs/agent-desktop, NVIDIA/auto-ontology, and thedotmack/claude-mem all address different layers of agent middleware, while anthropics/skills signals platform-level investment.

themes.name: Embodied AI Evaluation
themes.description: RoboColosseum and Democratizing Robot-Use Agents force a reckoning in how physical AI is benchmarked, revealing that cross-embodiment generalization — not single-task performance — is the true frontier challenge.

themes.name: Agent Safety & Governance
themes.description: Voluntary Servitude (NeurIPS 2026) exposes a new class of agent vulnerabilities, while microsoft/agent-governance-toolkit and Phantom Consensus highlight that multi-agent systems require dedicated safety frameworks beyond individual model alignment.

themes.name: Test-Time Compute & Reasoning
themes.description: Strategist, AIM, and Phantom Consensus all address how inference-time computation can be allocated more intelligently, with NeurIPS 2026 as the focal venue. The community is moving from "think longer" to "think smarter."

themes.name: Local & Edge AI
themes.description: FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c's proof that a 2.78T MoE runs on 8GB CPU challenges the GPU-cluster assumption, alongside FlashSSM-3D for edge 3D reconstruction, signaling a new wave of commodity-hardware deployments.

themes.name: 3D Generation & Understanding
themes.description: Frontier3DBench, Qwen3.5-4B-3D-Coder, FlashSSM-3D, and scenario-labs/skills all point to 3D as an emerging AI application tier — from coding agents that write ThreeJS to neural reconstruction on edge devices.
